title: Sit, Stay, Think
series: Sit, Stay, Think, an illustrated essay on measuring dog and cat minds
style: felted fur on warm cream: animals made of thousands of short curly wool hairs with tiny ink faces and pink blush, felt-ball data marks, yarn lines, Fraunces display type with Nunito Sans and IBM Plex Mono
context: The video explains how dog and cat 'IQ' and 'EQ' are measured and what breed rankings mean, following the essay Sit, Stay, Think. Coren 1994 (The Intelligence of Dogs): survey of 199 AKC/CKC obedience judges (a press report says 208), about 130 breeds in 79 ranks; measures working/obedience intelligence (trainability), one of three kinds (instinctive, adaptive, working). Top 10: Border Collie, Poodle, German Shepherd, Golden Retriever, Doberman, Shetland Sheepdog, Labrador, Papillon, Rottweiler, Australian Cattle Dog. Bottom: Shih Tzu 70, Basset 71, Mastiff and Beagle 72, Pekingese 73, Bloodhound 74, Borzoi 75, Chow Chow 76, Bulldog 77, Basenji 78, Afghan Hound 79. Top tier learns a new command in <5 repetitions and obeys first command 95%+; bottom tier 80-100+ repetitions, 25% or less. 190 of 199 judges put the Border Collie in their top ten. Clever Hans 1904 (Pfungst): 89% correct when he could see the questioner, 6% when not; 98% vs 8% when the questioner knew or did not know the answer. Thorndike 1898 puzzle boxes: cat 12 took 160 s at first, ~6-7 s by trial 24. IQ coined by William Stern 1912. Lab batteries test single skills: pointing, cylinder (inhibitory control), memory, reasoning. Gnanadesikan 2020: 1,508 dogs, 36 breeds; among-breed heritability inhibitory control 0.70 (0.50 after body size), communication 0.39, physical reasoning 0.21, memory 0.17. Horschler 2019: 7,397 dogs, 74 breeds; larger-brained breeds better at short-term memory and self-control. Junttila 2022 Finland: 1,002 dogs; Border Collies best at cylinder, Kelpies and Malinois at gestures; no breed differences in logic or memory. Arden & Adams 2016: g factor in 68 Border Collies explains 17%. MacLean 2019: 14,000+ dogs, 101 breeds, trainability among-breed heritability 0.73, mean 0.51. Morrill 2022 (Science): 18,385 dogs, 2,155 genotyped; breed explains ~9% of individual behaviour (3-25%). Ghirlanda 2013: popularity unrelated to behaviour. Chaser the Border Collie learned 1,022 object names; only 1 of 34 typical dogs learned two toy names in three months vs 6 of 6 gifted dogs. Dog EQ: no validated EQ test; C-BARQ owner questionnaire (152 items 2003, 78 in MacLean 2019). Kaminski 2019: inner-eyebrow muscle LAOM in dogs, scant in wolves. Albuquerque 2016: 17 dogs matched emotional voice to face in 67% of trials. Custance & Mayer 2012: 15 of 18 dogs approached a crying person. Harris & Prouvost 2014: ~25% of 36 dogs snapped at a stuffed dog the owner petted. Cats: Miklosi 2005: 7 of 26 recruited cats dropped out; 14 cats, 14 dogs; equal at pointing; unsolvable task 12/14 dogs vs 6/14 cats looked back at a human. Saito 2019: cats discriminate their own names. Vitale 2019: 64.3% of 70 kittens and 65.8% of 38 adult cats securely attached, infants ~65%. Merola 2015: 79% of cats social-referenced the owner. Quaranta 2020: 10 cats matched human emotions. Salonen 2019: 5,726 cats, 40 breeds, temperament differences (Korat people-oriented, Russian Blue shyest, Turkish Van most aggressive, Bengal active), no cognition measured; no evidence-based cat-breed intelligence ranking. Registries recognise 45-75 cat breeds. Brains: encephalization quotient (Jerison) cat 1.0, dog 1.2 (1.2-2.4 by breed), human 7.4-7.8. Jardim-Messeder 2017: cortical neurons cat ~250 million (one cat), dog ~528 million (two dogs; golden retriever 627 M), brown bear 251 million.
